documents.title: Single-cell Morphological Mechanisms-of-Action Profiling using Nanowell Imaging Plates.
documents.abstract: Mechanism-of-action (MoA) analysis is used in drug discovery to prioritize compounds that act through desired pathways while eliminating compounds associated with nonspecific or undesirable activity. Image cytometry provides a promising route for MoA inference by capturing high-dimensional cellular phenotypes at single-cell resolution, but conventional workflows remain limited by unreliable cell segmentation and dependence on human-engineered feature extraction. Here, we present a deep learning-based image cytometry workflow that confines single cells in nanowells to obtain uniformly framed, r
documents.journal: SLAS discovery : advancing life sciences R & D

documents.title: Surrogate Machine Learning Models for ADME Prediction: From Synthetic Labels to Experimental Data.
documents.abstract: Optimization of absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) properties is central to small-molecule drug discovery, yet is often constrained by limited access to large and consistent experimental data sets. The performance and generalizability of machine learning (ML) models for ADME property prediction rely on the composition of the training data. Surrogate data sets comprise compounds annotated with synthetic ADME labels (predictions) generated by ML models trained on experimental data. This can offer a consistent data augmentation or sharing strategy without requiring access
documents.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling

documents.title: DrugMAP 3.0: an enriched molecular atlas featuring ADMET endpoints, pharmacogenomic perturbations, and bioactivity atlas of drugs.
documents.abstract: The paradigm of targeted therapeutics has shifted from static drug-target interactions to systemic absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) endpoints, dynamic transcriptomic perturbation signatures, and quantitative binding affinities, thereby amplifying the demand for multidimensional pharmacological atlases. In other words, it is necessary to bridge systemic safety profiles, cellular responses, and molecular interactions. However, such integrative data were inadequately covered by existing databases. In this study, DrugMAP was therefore substantially updated, whi

documents.title: AI-Driven Discovery of Nodakenin as a Novel Molecular Glue Targeting the TRIM28-NR4A1-LCN2 Axis to Induce Ferroptosis in Melanoma.
documents.abstract: Melanoma remains a malignancy requiring novel interventions. While triggering ferroptosis has emerged as a promising anti-tumor strategy, the targetable molecular vulnerabilities governing this process remain incompletely understood. Here, through artificial intelligence (AI)-driven virtual screening, we identified the coumarin derivative Nodakenin (NK) as a potent inhibitor of nuclear receptor subfamily 4 group A member 1 (NR4A1), an orphan nuclear receptor highly expressed in malignant melanoma cells. Transcriptomic, biochemical, and structural analyses revealed that NK triggers ferroptosis

documents.title: Targeting protein degradation strategies in drug discovery: integrating PROTACs, ubiquitination biology, and AI-driven design.
documents.abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a transformative therapeutic strategy for eliminating disease-associated proteins, including targets that remain challenging to modulate using conventional occupancy-driven inhibitors. Among TPD approaches, proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) exploit the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) to induce selective and event-driven degradation of proteins of interest (POIs). Despite rapid advances in PROTAC development, successful translation depends on interconnected determinants, including target degradability, ubiquitin ligase (E3) recruitment,

documents.title: Existing Drugs Targeting Genes of Hereditary Pain Syndromes as Candidates for Analgesic Repurposing: An AI-Facilitated Computational Knowledge Discovery Analysis.
documents.abstract: Background/Objectives: Over the last few decades, hereditary syndromes with extreme pain phenotypes have guided the discovery of analgesic drugs. We hypothesized that genes of hereditary syndromes with altered pain perception, not necessarily the extreme phenotypes grouped as hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathies, could also point to existing drugs with unrecognized analgesic properties via known interactions with syndrome-relevant gene products. Methods: Phenotypes with altered pain mentions were retrieved from the Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) database, and their genes w

documents.title: From Gene Lists to Druggable Hubs: An Integrative In Silico Framework for Alternative Lengthening of Telomeres.
documents.abstract: Between 10 and 15% of cancers maintain their telomeres without telomerase, through a recombination-based route known as alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT). It is most common in sarcomas and gliomas. The mechanism itself is increasingly well understood, but the view from population-scale data is not: which components are perturbed most consistently across tumors, how they organize into networks, what they cost the cell metabolically, whether their expression says anything about outcome, and which existing drugs might exploit them. Here we bring together four in silico studies that used

documents.title: Phytochemical Profiling and Biological Activities of Moroccan Juniperus phoenicea L. Leaf Extracts: UHPLC-MS Analysis, Molecular Docking, and ADMET Predictions.
documents.abstract: Juniperus phoenicea L. is a medicinal plant native to the Mediterranean region, including Morocco, where it is traditionally used to treat various ailments. This study aimed to characterize the phytochemical profiles of aqueous, ethanolic, and hydroethanolic leaf extracts of Moroccan J. phoenicea and evaluate their antioxidant, antibacterial, and antifungal activities. Potential interactions between the extracts and conventional antimicrobial agents were also investigated, alongside molecular docking analyses of selected phytochemicals and in silico predictions of their pharmacokinetic and tox

documents.title: Multi-Target Anti-Inflammatory Mechanisms of Stachyurus praecox Leaf Extract Revealed by Metabolomics, Network Pharmacology, Molecular Docking, and Experimental Validation.
documents.abstract: Inflammation is a major pathological process underlying numerous chronic diseases, highlighting the need for anti-inflammatory inhibitors from nature. This study investigated the anti-inflammatory potential of S. praecox leaf extracts and elucidated molecular mechanisms through an integrated experimental and computational approach. As a result, the 75% methanol extract (75M) inhibited tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) production in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW264.7. Untargeted metabolomic analysis led to the tentative identification of 96 metabolites, predomin

documents.title: Computational Hazard Prioritization of Aerosolized E-Cigarette Flavoring Additives Using Virtual Knockout, Molecular Dynamics, and Human Genetic Follow-Up.
documents.abstract: Background/Objectives: Inhaled e-cigarette flavoring additives contact oral and respiratory epithelia, yet chemical-specific testing priorities and molecular hypotheses remain scarce. We combined chemical-screening and contextual gene-level branches to nominate priority flavorings and testable pathway hypotheses. Methods: Eight flavoring additives and carrier solvents were evaluated across 229 shared targets and 29 hubs via an 80-pair AutoDock Vina screen (exhaustiveness = 32), reference-inhibitor redocking, AlphaFold 3/Protein Data Bank checks, replicated 100 ns molecular dynamics, and ADMET/

documents.title: Computational Prediction of Elbasvir as a Theoretical Candidate for PFOS-Associated Gut and Skin Shared Pathologies.
documents.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) frequently co-occur along the gut-skin axis, yet the systemic triggers, particularly environmental endocrine-disrupting chemicals like perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS), remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate network toxicology and single-cell multi-omics to propose a computational framework for the shared molecular signatures of PFOS-driven AD and IBD comorbidity. Utilizing large-scale clinical transcriptomic cohorts and machine learning, we computationally predicted the transcription factor MYC as a potential core pathologic

documents.title: Molecularly Aged Protein States as Targets for Drug Design and Delivery in Neurodegenerative Diseases.
documents.abstract: Neurodegenerative drug discovery usually represents a protein target by its gene, canonical sequence, and one or a few structures. That representation can miss the molecular history accumulated by proteins that persist in the brain. Spontaneous chemistry, incomplete repair, altered turnover, proteolysis, phase transitions, and assembly remodeling generate states that may differ from the canonical target in exposure, function, and therapeutic accessibility. We call compositionally resolved species age-generated proteoforms and use molecularly aged protein states when the exact composition remai

documents.title: In Silico and In Vitro Studies on Selective MAO-B Inhibition and Predicted Microbiome Interactions of Novel Chalcone Derivatives: Relevance to the Gut-Brain Axis in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
documents.abstract: Background/Objectives: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) lacks pharmacological therapies for its core features. This study synthesized chalcone derivatives, determined their monoamine oxidase A (MAO-A) and MAO-B inhibitory profiles, and generated computational hypotheses regarding MAO-B binding, gut-bacterial protein interactions, and drug-like properties. Methods: Sixteen chalcones (23-38; fifteen newly reported) were synthesized and characterized. MAO-A and MAO-B inhibition was measured using fluorometric concentration-response assays, with clorgyline and safinamide as references. Compounds 23,

documents.title: Antioxidants from Onion (Allium cepa L.): Current Evidence, Redox Mechanisms, and an AI-Assisted Discovery Framework.
documents.abstract: Allium cepa L. (onion) is a globally important vegetable crop and functional food recognized for its rich diversity of antioxidant phytochemicals, including flavonoids, organosulfur compounds, phenolic acids, anthocyanins, saponins, and polysaccharides. Onion-derived phytochemicals have demonstrated antioxidant and redox-modulating activities in chemical, cellular, and animal studies. However, onion-specific applications of artificial intelligence and structure-based computational methods remain limited. This review therefore discriminates established experimental evidence from computational p

documents.title: Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability Prediction: Machine Learning, Graph Neural Networks, and Protonation-State Robustness.
documents.abstract: Blood-brain barrier permeability (BBBP) prediction is important for central nervous system (CNS) drug discovery, yet the relative performance of traditional molecular feature-based models and graph neural networks (GNNs), as well as the sensitivity of BBBP predictions to molecular protonation states, remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we curated the public OmniBBBP dataset through structural deduplication, label-conflict resolution, and removal of compounds overlapping with an external benchmark, yielding 8836 compounds for model development. Four traditional machine learning (ML) mod

documents.title: Machine Learning and Structure-Based Virtual Screening for Reliability-Aware G Protein-Coupled Receptor Ligand Prioritization.
documents.abstract: Background: Predictive performance is necessary but insufficient for G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) ligand prioritization, where heterogeneous bioactivity data, analog-series overlap, receptor-state dependence, and polypharmacology can weaken high-scoring predictions. Methods: We developed an auditable ligand- and structure-based workflow across five human GPCRs: DRD2, CB2, ADORA2A, OPRM1, and CCR5. ChEMBL Ki, IC50, and EC50 data were evaluated using scaffold-disjoint validation, external validation, Venn-Abers calibration, conformal prediction, applicability-domain analysis, explainability

documents.title: Toll-Like Receptors in Mycoplasma Infections: Immunopathogenesis, Cheminformatics, and Machine Learning-Based Insights into TLR-Targeted Therapeutics.
documents.abstract: Mycoplasma species are the minimal-genome pathogens that elicit complex host immune responses involving both protective and pathogenic inflammation. Toll-like receptors (TLRs) are pivotal components of the immune system, recognizing pathogen-associated molecular patterns and damage-associated molecular patterns to initiate immune responses. TLRs recognize Mycoplasma-derived lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA motifs, initiating NF-κB and MAPK signaling cascades. While these pathways are indispensable for microbial clearance, their dysregulation contributes to chronic inflammation, auto

documents.title: Pharmaceutical Methotrexate Formulation Exposure Alters Growth and Biofilm of Pseudomonas aeruginosa with Exploratory Evidence for Folate-Pathway Involvement.
documents.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa remains challenging to control because of intrinsic antimicrobial resistance and biofilm-associated tolerance, highlighting the need to explore alternative therapeutic strategies. This study investigated the in vitro effects of a pharmaceutical methotrexate (MTX) formulation on P. aeruginosa PAO1, its interaction with gentamicin (GEN), and the potential relevance of selected folate-pathway proteins. Planktonic growth inhibition, growth kinetics, developing and preformed biofilm biomass, and biofilm-associated membrane integrity were evaluated. MTX-GEN interactions were e

documents.title: Benchmarking Structural Models of α-Conotoxin-Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptor Complexes: Apo-Conformer Selection, Interface Information, and Deep-Learning Co-Folding.
documents.abstract: Conopeptides are a proven drug source, but translation stalls at one step: predicting how a peptide engages a human receptor before a clinical program commits. We benchmarked modelling of α-conotoxin-nicotinic acetylcholine receptor complexes at two deposited structures, kept separate because their data-leakage status differs: a human α7-ImI cryo-EM complex, rated MEDIUM leakage risk, and a non-human Aplysia acetylcholine-binding protein-RgIA crystal that lies inside the Boltz-2 training window and is therefore a positive control, not a held-out test. Apo-conformer choice fixes attainable accu

documents.title: Phytochemical Profiling and Preliminary In Vitro Assessment of Thai Traditional Medicine (Yahom Navakot) Extracts on HepG2 Cells, Integrated with ADMET and Molecular Docking Analyses of Selected Identified Compounds.
documents.abstract: Yahom Navakot (NV) is a traditional Thai polyherbal formulation with a long history of use in traditional medicine. However, its hepatoprotective potential and chemical characteristics remain incompletely characterized. This study investigated the biological activities and chemical profiles of aqueous and methanolic NV extracts using complementary in vitro and in silico approaches. The aqueous and methanolic extracts maintained human hepatocellular carcinoma (HepG2) cell viability above 70% at 25-400 µg/mL. In a hydrogen peroxide (H2O2)-induced oxidative stress model, the methanolic extract at

documents.title: In Silico Identification of a Potential Multi-Target Natural Compound Against Oral Cancer.
documents.abstract: Oral cancer remains a significant global health problem due to delayed diagnosis and limited treatment effectiveness. This study employed an integrated in silico approach to identify potential natural compounds from the family Ganodermataceae, targeting chemokine receptors CXCR3, CXCR4 and CXCR7. A library of 1300 mushroom-derived compounds was screened using a ligand-based pharmacophore. The best hits were subjected to molecular docking. The computational candidate, (+)-Applanatumol D, was further evaluated using ADMET, DFT, 200 ns MD simulations and MM-GBSA. Molecular docking predicted inter

documents.title: Target-Specific Benchmarking of Potency Prediction on Activity-Cliff Compounds Across 33 Human Protein Targets Using Inhibition Constants.
documents.abstract: Activity cliffs are pairs of closely related compounds whose potencies differ far more than their structures suggest, and the compounds involved in them remain a leading cause of local failure in ligand-based potency prediction. The MoleculeACE benchmark established that models predict these compounds poorly and that the gap differs between datasets. What has been missing is a panel built on one activity endpoint, a per-target account of how large the gap is, and a measurement of how far it depends on the way the model is chosen. We curated inhibition constant (Ki) data for 33 human protein ta

documents.title: Genome-Wide CRISPR Screening Identifies NAPRT as a Key Regulator of Human Adipogenesis.
documents.abstract: Adipocyte differentiation is central to adipose-tissue homeostasis, but its regulatory landscape remains incompletely defined in human cells. Here, we perform a genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screen in oleic acid-differentiated human SW872 preadipocytes to identify functional regulators of white adipogenesis. The screens nominate hundreds of adipogenesis-regulating genes, and integration with human genetic evidence prioritizes nicotinate phosphoribosyltransferase (NAPRT) as a prominent player. NAPRT loss increases lipid accumulation and PPARγ abundance, reduces intracellular nicotinamide ade

documents.title: Integrated Experimental and Computational Discovery of the Oxazole-Thiadiazole-Sulfonamide Hybrids as Dual α-Amylase and α-Glucosidase Inhibitors.
documents.abstract: Background: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a major global health concern. Inhibition of α-amylase and α-glucosidase is an established approach to controlling postprandial glucose levels. In this study, we aimed to synthesize oxazole-thiadiazole-sulphonamide derivatives (1-14) and evaluate their inhibitory activity against both enzymes. Methods: Fourteen derivatives were synthesized and characterized using 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and high-resolution electron ionization mass spectrometry (HR-EI-MS). Their inhibitory activities were evaluated using acarbose as the reference inhibitor. Structure-activity rela

documents.title: ATC Classification and Scaffold-Split pMIC Prediction for Antibacterial Prioritization.
documents.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance requires reproducible computational tools that distinguish antibacterial-drug class membership from measured antibacterial potency. We developed a descriptor-based workflow for Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical classification (ATC)-based prioritization, exploratory molecular generation, and pMIC prediction.

documents.title: Screening and Evaluation of Computationally Predicted JAK1-Binding Candidates from Multi-Source Chemical Space Using Deep Learning and Generative Models.
documents.abstract: Background/Objectives: Janus kinase 1 (JAK1) is a key mediator in inflammatory and autoimmune signaling pathways and represents a validated therapeutic target. Despite the availability of several JAK inhibitors, challenges in safety and efficacy persist, necessitating further computational prioritization of candidate molecules. Methods: We developed an integrated virtual screening workflow combining ensemble deep learning scoring (KPGT, KarmaDock, DrugCLIP), ADMET-AI filtering, and AutoDock Vina (v1.2.3) docking. The workflow was applied to the NPBS Atlas natural-product database and to molecu

documents.title: Accelerating MAPK1 Inhibitor Discovery Through Stacking Ensemble Learning with Graph Neural Networks.
documents.abstract: Mitogen-activated protein kinase 1 (MAPK1) plays a central role in cancer cell proliferation and survival. In this study, we developed an ensemble graph neural network framework integrating graph convolutional neural networks, graph message-passing neural networks, and attention-based graph neural networks to predict MAPK1 inhibitory activity using large-scale quantitative high-throughput screening data. Our models achieved recall ranging from 79.5% to 92.3%, areas under the precision-recall curve ranging from 80.4% to 90.3%, and Matthews correlation coefficients ranging from 0.523 to 0.725 on

documents.title: Learning inhibitor interactions from protein deep mutational scanning data and deep learning models.
documents.abstract: Recent advances in protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction frameworks have the potential to accelerate computational drug discovery. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond their training sets. Mutation-dependent drug responses present a challenge to these methods because there are often large effects from relatively small perturbations. Here, we systematically benchmark diverse mutational effect and drug-target affinity prediction models using deep mutational scanning datasets spanning 11 inhibitor conditions for the MET kinase d
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Theoretical and Chromatographic Studies to Determine Selected Physicochemical Parameters of 8-Trifluoromethylquinobenzothiazines as Potential Bioactive Compounds.
documents.abstract: Chemical modification of the phenothiazine structure enables the synthesis of promising molecules that are potential candidates for new drugs with a broad spectrum of biological activity. Both computational and experimental methods play a crucial role in the preliminary study of new bioactive compounds, serving to determine various physicochemical properties that influence a compound's ADMET profile, including its lipophilicity.

documents.title: NFKBIA as a Potential Aging-Related Comorbidity Gene Linking Renal Fibrosis and Age-Associated Muscle Dysfunction: A Hypothesis-Generating Multi-Omics Analysis with Tissue-Specific Regulatory Patterns.
documents.abstract: Aging accelerates renal fibrosis (RF) and age-associated muscle dysfunction (muscle aging), but their shared mechanisms remain unclear. We integrated multi-omics bioinformatics to identify aging-related comorbidity genes linking RF and muscle aging. Bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) used estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and appendicular lean mass (ALM) as proxies for kidney function and muscle mass, followed by differential expression analysis, four machine learning algorithms (LASSO, SVM-RFE, Random Forest, XGBoost), single-cell transcriptomics, pseudotime order

documents.title: Computational Identification and Prioritization of Novel Tankyrase 1 and 2 Inhibitor Candidates Through Structure-Based Design, ADMET Profiling, and Long-Timescale Molecular Dynamics.
documents.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains one of the most aggressive breast cancer subtypes and is frequently associated with aberrant activation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. Because tankyrase 1 and 2 (TNKS1/2) promote Wnt pathway activation through the regulation of AXIN stability, these enzymes represent attractive therapeutic targets for the development of novel anticancer agents. In this study, an integrated structure-based computational workflow was employed to identify new TNKS1/2 inhibitors. A library comprising known tankyrase inhibitors, structurally related analogues, a

documents.title: Repurposing of Conivaptan as a Novel Quorum Sensing Inhibitor Against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
documents.abstract: Background: The emergence of multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P. aeruginosa) poses a significant clinical challenge, necessitating innovative anti-infective strategies. Through high-throughput virtual screening of the DrugBank database, this study identified Conivaptan (hydrochloride, C32H27ClN4O2), an FDA-approved anti-hyponatremia drug, as a potential quorum-sensing inhibitor targeting key regulatory proteins (LasR, RhlR, and PqsR) of P. aeruginosa. Methods: Molecular docking was performed to assess binding interactions with QS regulators. Transcriptomic analysis (RNA-seq) and qua

documents.title: From Generative Biology to Evidence-Centric Drug Discovery.
documents.abstract: Generative and predictive artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly increasing the number of molecular, structural, cellular, and therapeutic hypotheses that can be explored computationally. Experimental capacity, however, has not expanded at a comparable rate. The result is an evidence bottleneck, in which biological hypotheses are generated faster than they can be experimentally tested, reproduced, and translated. This mismatch is particularly consequential for pharmaceutical discovery, where computational predictions alone cannot establish biological function, mechanism, or therapeutic value.

documents.title: Thiazolyl-Methylthio-1,3,4-Thiadiazolyl-Quinazolin-4(3H)-ones Hybrids: Synthesis, In Silico Profiling, Cytotoxicity, Cellular Death Evaluation, and Effects on Irradiation-Associated DNA Damage.
documents.abstract: Background/Objectives: Combining heterocyclic fragments provides a strategy for developing compounds for exploratory anticancer evaluation. This study aimed to synthesize and characterize five thiazolyl-methylthio-1,3,4-thiadiazolyl-quinazolin-4(3H)-one compounds (5a-e), assess their properties in silico, and investigate the selected ones for cytotoxicity and their effects on irradiation-associated DNA lesions. Methods: Structures were characterized by IR, HRMS, and 1H- and 13C-NMR spectroscopy. Computational studies included physicochemical and ADMETox predictions, multi-platform target predi

documents.title: RepurposeAD: Knowledge Graph-Guided LLM Reasoning for Alzheimer's Drug Repurposing.
documents.abstract: Background/Objectives: Alzheimer's disease (AD) drug development continues to suffer from high late-stage attrition and narrow mechanistic diversity, which makes the systematic repurposing of approved compounds an urgent priority. Existing computational repurposing methods operate on fragmented biomedical knowledge, rarely integrate transcriptomic and pharmacological evidence within a single reasoning process, and provide little of the mechanistic transparency required for clinical translation. This paper presents RepurposeAD, a knowledge graph-guided large language model (LLM) reasoning frame

documents.title: Characterization and Evaluation of the Neuroprotective Potential of Peptides Derived from Holothuria scabra Inner Wall Proteins: An In Vitro Study.
documents.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are characterized by progressive neuronal dysfunction driven by interconnected mechanisms, including oxidative stress, apoptosis, and impaired protein homeostasis. Marine-derived proteins and peptides represent promising sources of multifunctional neuroprotective agents; however, the neuroprotective potential of gastrointestinal digestion-derived peptides from Holothuria scabra remains poorly characterized. This study investigated the neuroprotective effects of a gastrointestinal digest of H. scabra inner-wall proteins (IWD), a mixture of digestion-derived peptides,

documents.title: From Computational Prioritization to Material Supply: A Proposed Two-Axis Record for Marine Invertebrate-Associated Natural Products and Derivatives.
documents.abstract: Marine natural products can show biological activity while remaining difficult to identify, reproduce, or obtain in sufficient quantity. This critical narrative review examines that mismatch and proposes a linked record for each exact chemical entity-indication pair. The documented evaluation stage (E1-E4) records computational, in vitro, animal, or human evaluation; the production/access stage (S1-S5) records physical access, an executed laboratory route, controlled pilot production, good manufacturing practice (GMP) clinical manufacture, or established commercial manufacture. Neither coordin

documents.title: Morus Prenylflavonoids as Candidate NLRP3 Inflammasome Inhibitors from an AI-Guided Natural-Product Screen with a Quantified Applicability Domain.
documents.abstract: Background/Objectives: The NLRP3 (NACHT, LRR and PYD domains-containing protein 3) inflammasome drives interleukin-1β maturation and pyroptosis in chronic inflammatory disease, and no direct inhibitor has been approved. Natural products are a plausible source of new chemical matter for this target, but such collections are too large to dock exhaustively, and the machine-learning rankings used to triage them are routinely acted on without stating the chemistry over which they hold. This study prioritises natural-product candidates for NLRP3 while quantifying that limit explicitly. Methods: In t

documents.title: Multi-Cohort Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Analyses Identify Six Directionally Concordant Blood-Transcriptomic Signals Associated with Low Bone Mineral Density and Alzheimer's Disease.
documents.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and low bone mineral density (BMD) frequently coexist, but whether they show reproducible concordant blood-transcriptomic signals remains unclear. We conducted a retrospective computational study to identify cross-phenotype expression patterns and explore their biological context.

documents.title: Single-Cell eQTL Mendelian Randomization and Colocalization Analysis Reveals Immune Cell-Specific Genetic Insights into Functional Dyspepsia.
documents.abstract: Background Functional dyspepsia (FD) is a common gastrointestinal disorder characterized by multiple clinical symptoms, complex pathophysiology, and limited therapeutic agents. Emerging evidence indicates a role for immune dysregulation in the pathogenesis of FD; however, immune cell-specific gene regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the genetic factors specific to different immune cell types in FD to explore promising therapeutic targets. Methods We performed Mendelian randomization (MR) and Bayesian colocalization analyses integrating single-cell expression quantitat

documents.title: Biophysical and Computational Evidence for Ibuprofen Binding to and Inhibition of MARK4.
documents.abstract: MARK4 is a serine/threonine kinase implicated in neurodegenerative disorders and cancer, making it an attractive target for therapeutic intervention and drug repurposing. In this study, we investigated the inhibition and interaction of ibuprofen with MARK4 using an integrated experimental and computational approach employing steady-state fluorescence and UV-vis spectroscopy, circular dichroism, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations. The ATPase assays showed that ibuprofen produces dose-dependent inhibition of MARK4 ATPase activity. The ATPase activity of MARK4 was inhibited by

documents.title: ADMET-Stack: quantitative guidance on how much representational complexity an ADMET endpoint actually requires.
documents.abstract: Accurate absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) prediction determines whether a drug candidate survives early development, yet how well it can be predicted depends heavily on how molecules are represented. Previous studies have generally focused on new model architectures, with less attention to the effects of molecular representations and features on ADMET prediction. Here, we evaluated 54 combinations of structural fingerprints, physicochemical descriptors, and SELFIES-derived encodings across all 22 ADMET endpoints of the Therapeutics Data Commons (TDC) Leader

documents.title: Survival of the fittest tool: choosing between open and closed artificial intelligence in pharmaceutical science.
documents.abstract: Three years ago, this journal published the editorial Technological Darwinism, urging pharmaceutical scientists to adapt to artificial intelligence (AI) rather than resist it. Since then, the question has shifted from whether to use AI to which AI to use, under what circumstances, and with what evidence. This review addresses that question by mapping current AI tools across the five canonical stages of drug development, from discovery to post-market pharmacovigilance. It is a narrative review, not a systematic one, and it treats openness as a spectrum rather than a binary. It compares two broa
documents.journal: Journal of pharmacy & pharmaceutical sciences : a publication of the Canadian Society for Pharmaceutical Sciences, Societe canadienne des sciences pharmaceutiques

documents.title: Identification and characterization of ion channel-related signatures in ulcerative colitis: an integrated multi-omics and machine learning analysis.
documents.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic, multifactorial inflammatory bowel disease characterized by persistent mucosal inflammation and immune dysregulation. Human ion channel genes (HICGs) are involved in maintaining cellular homeostasis and regulating immune function, but their expression patterns and diagnostic value in UC have not been systematically investigated. This study aimed to identify UC-associated HICGs and evaluate their potential as diagnostic biomarkers using an integrative multi-omics approach.

documents.title: GPCRVS in the detection of target-selective molecular scaffolds based on deep learning and gradient boosting.
documents.abstract: High drug selectivity minimizes unintended interactions that cause adverse effects, decreases drug potency, and are failure-prone factors in many clinical trials due to a poor balance between drug efficacy and toxicity. Sharing similar structural folds and modes of activation, G protein-coupled receptors (GPCR) may represent difficult drug targets in terms of optimization of pharmacodynamic profiles towards drug target selectivity. Here, we describe GPCRVS, a web service for GPCR virtual screening, designed to detect selective drug-like compounds. GPCRVS combines machine learning for ligand-ba

documents.title: From AI-Generated Sequences to Therapeutic Peptide Candidates: A Disease-First Perspective on Computational Design, Developability, and Application.
documents.abstract: Therapeutic peptides bridge the gap between small-molecule drugs and biologics, offering high target selectivity and broad opportunities for chemical and structural optimization. However, their clinical translation remains constrained by proteolytic instability, limited bioavailability, delivery barriers, safety concerns, and manufacturing challenges. Artificial intelligence (AI) expands the generation and prioritization of peptide hypotheses through language models, target-conditioned design, structure-aware modeling, and multi-objective optimization. Experimental testing of disease-relevant

documents.title: AI-driven transformation of GPCR research: from structural biology to precision medicine.
documents.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) regulate complex pathophysiological networks and represent a critical class of drug targets, but their structural determination and ligand screening are constrained by dependence on homology templates, static conformations, and a bias toward known ligands. Artificial intelligence is fundamentally transforming GPCR structural biology and pharmacology by overcoming these bottlenecks. The methodologies encompass high-precision static structure prediction, dynamic conformational ensemble modeling, ultra-large-scale virtual screening, de novo ligand design, allos

documents.title: Identification of potential natural PPARγ agonists via graph neural networks and integrated computational approaches.
documents.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus has become a prevalent metabolic disease worldwide. Current synthetic PPARγ (Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ)agonists are associated with adverse effects, highlighting the need to explore natural compounds with potential PPARγ agonistic activity. PPARγ is a vital therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes. To facilitate the discovery of natural PPARγ agonists, this study integrated graph neural network (GNN) prediction, molecular docking, ADMET evaluation, in vitro activity assessment, and molecular dynamics simulations for multistage virtual screening. Three

documents.title: A Machine-Learning Framework Integrating Frequency-Domain Spectral Features for Ligand Classification and Candidate Prioritization.
documents.abstract: AI-assisted drug discovery (AIDD) combines molecular modeling with machine learning to support lead identification and candidate prioritization. Conventional molecular descriptors principally encode static chemical structures, leaving frequency-domain behavior as an additional source of molecular information. We therefore developed the terahertz fusion descriptor (THz-FD), a feature-fusion framework that integrates terahertz (THz) frequency-domain features for Na+/K+-ATPase ligand classification and retrospective ranking. Extra Trees (ET), Random Forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM) c

documents.title: An integrated computational and experimental framework identifies apigenin as a potential therapeutic agent targeting EGFR/STAT3/MMP9 signaling in glioma.
documents.abstract: Glioma is the most common primary malignant tumor of the central nervous system and is characterized by aggressive progression, high recurrence rates, and limited therapeutic options. Apigenin, a naturally occurring flavonoid, exhibits promising anti-tumor properties; however, its molecular mechanisms in glioma remain insufficiently understood. To systematically identify the therapeutic targets and molecular mechanisms underlying apigenin-mediated anti-glioma activity through an integrated computational and experimental approach.
